items_missed: Never asked "How are you today?" after the opening greeting.
No agenda-setting statement (call length/structure) and no explicit "Sound good?" confirmation before jumping straight into discovery questions.
Never explicitly probed for special considerations — narrow hallways, tight turns, or long carries — at either storage unit, despite discussing access and floor level.
Completely skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech — no framing that consolidating loose items before move day shortens the job, no "take a carload" tip, no close for that section.
Never asked "Any other questions before I let you go?" at the end of the call.
Never stated branch hours or how to reach the company if the customer needs to make changes (only said "give us a call" generically).
Explained the No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) but never mentioned the 60¢/lb baseline valuation coverage alongside it.
No genuine rapport-building moment, humor, or acknowledgment of the customer's scattered/distracted state (side conversation, trouble finding addresses) beyond plowing through the checklist.
Delivered the pricing, inclusions, and all three differentiators back-to-back in one long run-on explanation rather than breaking it into clear, digestible pieces.
top_strength: Stayed patient and thorough through a genuinely messy discovery (customer was distracted, unsure of addresses, and juggling a side conversation about scheduling) while still nailing every pricing differentiator — No Worries Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and a clean no-hidden-fees pitch — and locked in a booking with no deposit despite the customer being noncommittal on the date.
coaching_note: Add the Save Your Ass prep speech before moving to booking — it was skipped entirely here, and even on a storage-to-storage move like this one (loose non-boxed items, ~15 estimated boxes) there was room to coach the customer toward consolidating ahead of time to shave billable hours off a $1,143 estimate.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and polite throughout with the customer's name used repeatedly and a warm farewell, but heavy filler ("mm-hmm") and few genuine affirmations kept the call transactional rather than building real rapport.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily fragmented and garbled on both sides (customer's speech especially), with frequent cross-talk and incomplete sentences, making it hard to confidently judge vocal tone from text alone — worth an audio spot-check.
